name: Home Assistant
description: Bounded Home Assistant REST states, metadata, history, calendars and explicitly confirmed equipment actions.

permissions.description: Single requests to an explicit user-owned Home Assistant origin. Protected bearer token. Equipment/service/state/event actions require exact operation confirmation; no discovery, subscriptions, token refresh or retries. Event ingress requires explicit administrator profiles, saved secret references and provider/relay setup. Installation never provisions subscriptions or executes trigger code.

State writes change the displayed state only, not physical actuation. definitions.name: Home Assistant button press
definitions.description: Home Assistant button press
definitions.documentation: Home Assistant button press. POST /api/services/button/press. One bounded request, no redirects, pagination loop, discovery or retries. Direct typed argument sockets and named result contracts; dynamic JSON limited to entity attributes, service selector/default/example metadata and event data. Requires confirmActions=true and confirmation exactly HOME ASSISTANT BUTTON-PRESS. May cause equipment actions or automation side effects. State writes change the displayed state only, not physical actuation. Origin must be canonical and user-owned; LAN HTTP additionally requires allowInsecureLanHttp=true and httpAcknowledgment exactly I ACCEPT LAN HTTP TOKEN EXPOSURE. Protected token via secret or RuntimeConnection credentials.accessToken/apiKey and builtin $connection. Response 1 MiB/1000 items, request 128 KiB, JSON depth 24, total deadline 100–30000 ms includes lookup and successful reader cancellation. History/logbook/calendar windows at most seven days. No live provider or hardware verification. Sources: https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/internals/rest-api/ https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.10.4/homeassistant/components/api/__init__.py https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.10.4/homeassistant/components/calendar/__init__.py https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/switch/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/fan/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/climate/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cover/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/input_boolean/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/input_number/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/input_select/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/input_text/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/scene/ https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/button/

ingressRequirements.name: Home Assistant webhooks
ingressRequirements.description: Home Assistant delivers manually configured authenticated HTTPS callbacks.
setupSteps: Install this reviewed package release; installation does not provision any event delivery.
Publish the existing ONF HTTP listener through a reviewed HTTPS proxy preserving raw JSON bytes and required authentication headers.
Save the callback secret in Infrastructure → Secrets; create an ingress profile for this package requirement using header token chosen for the Home Assistant RESTful Command.
Bind the intended trigger node to that profile, save its provider filters, and deliberately enable both workflow and entry.
Create a Home Assistant automation for state_changed or automation_triggered and call a RESTful Command with POST JSON, verified TLS, the ONF callback URL and configured secret header.

Serialize event_type, time_fired and data from the selected automation event; add a unique stable delivery_id for bounded ONF deduplication. State events require data.entity_id and old_state/new_state objects (null is valid on entity removal/creation).
Create the callback secret in Home Assistant secret storage and ONF Secrets; never place actual credentials or callback URLs in package manifests.
Authorize a synthetic provider delivery and inspect its accepted run; HTTP 202 proves admission only. Review provider retries and downstream idempotency.

Select saved node entry mode webhook explicitly; package metadata does not infer it. Create/select a profile for this exact installed requirement (installation.id + "/provider-events"), bind node.trigger.ingress.profileId, save the graph and deliberately enable workflow and entry only when setup is complete.
